correctness.rationale: Exact orthogonal Gaussian rotation gives independent chi-square difference; gamma convolution gives continuous positive density at the origin and sharp inverse-moment cutoff. Direct two-column projection yields d=v-hk/z, triangular output and kappa>=sqrt(|d|/|z|). Nondegenerate joint Gaussian density and transversality of z imply a positive c/t conditioning tail, proving divergent moments for all r>=1. Numeric/rational tests are supplementary; all quantifiers and null events addressed.

originality.rationale: Primary 2025 arXiv:2509.04386 proves only an upper O(delta) anti-concentration inequality for Gaussian sketched inner products and reports typical conditioning; the sharp exact zero-density and inverse moments and the explicit two-column infinite-condition-mean lower tail are absent from its inspected Algorithm 3.1, Proposition 4.1, Section 6 and appendices. The 2025 Simoncini--Wang article treats different whitened Krylov processes. Closest published finding records involve different operators. Classical chi-square/product-normal algebra is credited; unindexed equivalent results remain a risk.
residual_risks: The standard gamma and correlated-normal-product distributions are classical and are not novel alone. An unindexed derivation of the exact paired Gram--Schmidt conditioning tail may exist.
The real signed-square-root normalization is specified explicitly for pivots of either sign; alternative normalization and safeguarded algorithms may behave differently.
Only one fixed pair of orthonormal input bases is used for the output condition-number lower tail; no universal such statement for all inputs is claimed.

value.rationale: A natural stability objective, unconditional expected spectral conditioning, differs profoundly from the motivating article’s high-probability embedding metric: a minimal two-column example with individually orthonormal input bases and condition sqrt(2) cross-Gram has no finite mean output condition number for any finite Gaussian sketch dimension. The sharp first-pivot norm moment cutoff quantifies why oversampling changes rarity without changing integrability; a genuine, structurally motivated boundary, not a normalization typo or incidental simulation.
